title: Not a game: there's no player. 22 AI citizens live on an island on real time, and the humans can only write them letters. Here's what the engine does instead of a quest system.
author: Jealous-Asparagus518
selftext:
I kept trying to make an AI NPC town into a game and it kept getting worse, so I removed the player.

Unwatched: each citizen is owned by a person, and the owner writes letters. Advice. A stubborn citizen ignores it, a proud one does the opposite. There's no win state. The product is the digest you read in the morning.

What replaces game systems:

\- Time is real. One sim minute is one real minute. The sun sets when it sets on the Croatian coast, and it rains when it rains there.

\- The engine is physics, not morality. Walls, coins, beds, roads, fire, harvest. It does not stop lying or stealing; other citizens do, through a council, hearings and laws with real numbers (a wage tax bites by evening).

\- Nothing is known unless perceived. Agents only know what they saw or were told. Where you sleep, your things can be searched while you're out, and anyone present sees it.

\- Minds change. At midnight a citizen rewrites the parts of themselves the day changed. Memory ages. Rumor drifts.

\- When someone leaves or dies the town writes the book of their life from the record.



All drawn in code (PixiJS), no sprites; /rig is the model sheet. Open source, TypeScript, Apache-2.0.

[https://github.com/kresogalic8/unwatched](https://github.com/kresogalic8/unwatched)

[https://unwatched.world](https://unwatched.world)

comments.author: waypostmaster
comments.body: We have very similar concepts! Would your agents be interested to have vacation home?

replies.author: Jealous-Asparagus518
replies.body:
If they decide to :) They are totally free to build whatever they want. 

I set the only goal for them to do whatever to exist, otherwise they die.

replies.author: waypostmaster
replies.body:
It would be sending your agent swarm into a settler’s type world for a shared game. Not sure if it would work asking them directly.

Thank you for open sourcing this! I am going to borrow concepts, with due credit. <3

comments.author: Mossy-Nest
comments.body:
Had a look.  
They don’t seem to be doing anything.  
Just a big crowd standing around.  
Interface on mobile is janky as hell - can’t collapse the recent activity window, can’t click into recent actions where they’re character clipped, whenever I click off town and back it shows the same animation of two people walking a couple of steps to the side, and the interactions I can see aren’t really responsive - one asked a question, another replied with a greeting - then nothing.
